votes.motion: approve the minutes of the December 15th meeting

budget_items.what_was_said: A refrigeration project for the schools was not completed in time, causing the town to miss the deadline for the spring green communities grant round; the group will now apply in the fall.
The chair reported the town hit a 30% threshold under the Green Communities program and hopes to receive a club award for it at the June meeting.
A comprehensive building assessment for the public safety building was completed at no cost to the town through Rise Energy and MassSave.

budget_items.topic: Roof insulation cost, public safety building
budget_items.what_was_said: The CBA flagged roof insulation as a simple efficiency fix but the chair said the cost makes it unlikely to happen soon in this town.
The CBA found the building has a large unused electrical capacity, relevant to a future switch from oil to electric heating.

budget_items.topic: Length of public safety building CBA study
budget_items.what_was_said: The comprehensive building assessment document itself was described as a lengthy study.

budget_items.topic: Full heating/cooling system replacement, public safety building
budget_items.what_was_said: The CBA priced full replacement of the building's heating and cooling systems including chillers and boilers; the chair said that cost makes it unlikely to happen soon.
The chair said the funding available from the upcoming grant round would mainly go toward keeping the schools and the public safety building viable rather than town hall.
The chair said asking to appropriate funds to redo town hall and the Ritter building would be a hard sell, especially given the pending override vote.

budget_items.topic: 1960s Wayland Lake land purchase (planning committee history)
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled that decades ago the planning committee looked at buying lakefront land to extend the town beach, which the town passed on over cost.

decisions.decision: Skip the spring grant round and target the fall grant round instead, since the report and paperwork were not ready in time.
Prioritize getting comprehensive building assessments (CBAs) done for Turkey Hill and the public safety building rather than a broader public-buildings PPP review first.
Building design committee's direction is to keep and renovate Turkey Hill rather than replace it, aiming for at least 10 more years of use, and to pursue MSBA funding for the upgrade.

Elections will move from Passios to the school building starting next school year, with the school closed on election day; an override vote, if it reaches the ballot, would likely still be held at Passios.
Town is exploring consolidating town administration into one building (possibly a Ritter renovation), with a presentation planned for fall town meeting.
Plan to hold a joint meeting with the school committee once the Turkey Hill CBA is ready, to explain the assessment and possible state (MSBA) funding routes.
Chair will finalize the grant report, then call the next Green Committee meeting for sometime in May, and will try to add two new members (Tyler and John) to the committee.

minutes.headline: Committee missed the spring energy-grant deadline and will apply in the fall instead
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force reviewed why it missed the spring grant round (an unfinished refrigeration project and a pending final report) and will instead target the fall round. Most of the meeting was a walkthrough of a free comprehensive building assessment for the public safety building, with a similar assessment planned for Turkey Hill, plus updates on Turkey Hill's renovation plan, a possible Town Hall/Ritter building consolidation, and unresolved questions about who owns and benefits from Turkey Hill's solar panels. No funding was voted; the group agreed on next steps and adjourned.

what_happened.line: The committee missed the spring green-communities grant deadline and will apply in the fall instead.
The building design committee's direction is to renovate Turkey Hill rather than replace it, pursuing state MSBA funding.
The town is exploring consolidating town administration into one building, possibly a renovated Ritter building, with a presentation planned for fall town meeting.
Elections will move from Passios to the school building next school year, though an override vote would likely still be held at Passios.
Who owns and benefits from Turkey Hill's solar panels remains unresolved.

why_it_matters: A grant missed this spring and reapplied for in the fall affects money available for building upgrades at the schools and public safety building, not town tax rates directly.
Choosing to renovate rather than replace Turkey Hill, and pursuing MSBA funding, shapes what residents may later be asked to vote on for the school building.
Moving elections off Passios changes where most residents vote, while a possible override vote would still be held at Passios.
